answer.policy_title: InterQual® Clinical Criteria (CP: Procedures, Arthroscopy, Knee or Arthroscopic ACL Reconstruction)
answer.effective_date: Updated annually (InterQual criteria are integrated into Fallon's portal effective January 1, 2024)
criteria_quotes: Because InterQual® is a proprietary clinical decision support system, the exact copyrighted text of the criteria is not publicly published and cannot be directly quoted here.

Standard clinical indicators typically required by InterQual for ACL Reconstruction (CPT 29888) include: 1) Documented diagnosis of an ACL tear (confirmed by MRI or physical examination findings such as a positive Lachman or pivot-shift test); 2) Recurrent clinical instability (e.g., knee 'giving way' or giving out); 3) Failure of conservative management (such as physical therapy or bracing) or a clear explanation of why conservative management is inappropriate (e.g., a high-demand athletic or physical occupation); and 4) Absence of severe, advanced osteoarthritis in the knee joint.
answer.submission_route:
Written appeals can be submitted via: 
- Mail: Fallon Health, Member Appeals and Grievances, 1 Mercantile St., Ste. 400, Worcester, MA 01608 
- Fax: 1-508-755-7393 
- Email: grievance@fallonhealth.org 
Appeals can also be initiated by phone by calling the Member Appeals and Grievances Department at 1-800-333-2535, ext. 69950 (TRS 711) or general Customer Service at 1-800-868-5200.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: Because Fallon Health uses proprietary InterQual® criteria for procedures lacking a custom plan policy (such as ACL reconstruction under CPT 29888), these guidelines are not freely downloadable on the open internet. The patient can obtain a free, complete copy of the specific clinical coverage guidelines used to deny their care by contacting Fallon Health's Member Appeals and Grievances Department at 1-800-333-2535, ext. 69950 or Customer Service at 1-800-868-5200. Providers may also view the criteria by logging into the InterQual transparency tool on the Fallon Health provider portal (https://fallonhealth.org/en/providers/criteria-policies-guidelines.aspx).
answer.notes: A thorough search of Fallon Health's medical policy index confirms there is no insurer-specific, custom medical policy for ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888). Fallon Health explicitly references the use of InterQual® clinical criteria for determining the medical necessity of knee/orthopedic procedures not covered under plan-specific policies.

Member: Reese Iverson

Plan: Fallon Health (Commercial/ACA), state of Massachusetts

Dear Reese,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Procedure code (CPT): 29888

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-11).

Reference number: POC-19FF75EFC5-13767

results.snippet: The anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) is one of 2 cruciate ligaments that aids in stabilizing the knee joint. It is a strong band made of connective tissue and collagenous fibers that originate from the anteromedial aspect of the intercondylar region of the tibial plateau and extends posterolaterally to attach to the medial aspect of the lateral femoral condyle, where there are two important landmarks; The lateral intercondylar ridge which defines the anterior boundary of the ACL, and the bifurcate ridge which separates the 2 ACL bundles.

results.title: ACL reconstruction — orthopedic coding glossary | Mira Health
results.snippet: Selecting the wrong CPT code (e.g., billing open code 27407 for an arthroscopic case, or billing 29888 when a meniscal repair was bundled into the same code) triggers NCCI PTP edit denials and can escalate to post-payment audits. Separately, failing to distinguish an acute ACL tear from a chronic tear or a revision reconstruction in the ICD-10 diagnosis directly affects medical necessity review: payers routinely deny ACL reconstruction claims when the documented diagnosis reflects a chronic degenerative finding without supporting functional instability criteria, resulting in full claim write-offs that are difficult to overturn on appeal.

results.title: CPT Code 29888 Description, Scenarios & Applicable Modifiers
results.snippet: Orthopedic surgeons use this specialized instrument and imaging to perform the necessary surgical repair or reconstruction. The purpose of this surgery is to restore the function of the anterior cruciate ligament within the knee joint, which may be either slightly damaged or completely torn.
